chapters.title: Showing Up
chapters.sourcePressure: Separate initial selection from sustained return under pressure.
chapters.coreMove: Treat grit as the act of staying in the hard place after credentials stop helping.
chapters.commonMisread: Thinking grit means toughness, elite credentials, or one heroic burst.

chapters.title: Distracted by Talent
chapters.sourcePressure: Correct the habit of overreading quick aptitude and underreading repeated effort.
chapters.coreMove: Look past easy performance and ask who keeps improving when the work stops flattering them.
chapters.commonMisread: Thinking the point is that talent does not matter at all.

chapters.title: Effort Counts Twice
chapters.sourcePressure: Show why effort both builds skill and turns skill into achievement.
chapters.coreMove: Break achievement into skill-building effort and skill-using effort before judging outcomes.
chapters.commonMisread: Reducing the formula to work harder and ignoring the two separate jobs effort performs.

chapters.title: How Gritty Are You?
chapters.sourcePressure: Make grit observable as consistency of passion plus perseverance, not short-term strain.
chapters.coreMove: Audit whether a commitment has lasted long enough to count as direction instead of intensity.
chapters.commonMisread: Thinking a hard week, a startup sprint, or a high score proves grit.

chapters.title: Grit Grows
chapters.sourcePressure: Argue that grit is partly inherited but substantially shaped by experience.
chapters.coreMove: Move from asking whether you have grit to asking which conditions are growing or shrinking it.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating grit as either pure genetics or pure choice.

chapters.title: Interest
chapters.sourcePressure: Explain that durable passion usually begins as curiosity that is developed, not a lightning strike.
chapters.coreMove: Convert vague passion hunting into patient sampling, feedback, and repeated return.
chapters.commonMisread: Telling readers to quit everything and follow a perfect passion immediately.

chapters.title: Practice
chapters.sourcePressure: Distinguish deliberate practice from years of repetition.
chapters.coreMove: Choose one weak subskill, stretch it, seek feedback, and repeat until the miss changes.
chapters.commonMisread: Thinking practice means time served or mindless repetition.

chapters.title: Purpose
chapters.sourcePressure: Show how interest becomes more durable when tied to benefit beyond the self.
chapters.coreMove: Attach a personal craft to a real beneficiary so effort has a reason on bad days.
chapters.commonMisread: Turning purpose into lofty slogans detached from daily work.

chapters.title: Hope
chapters.sourcePressure: Define hope as belief that effort can improve the future after failure.
chapters.coreMove: Rewrite a setback from permanent identity evidence into a specific problem to work.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating hope as optimism, mood, or waiting for luck.

chapters.title: Parenting for Grit
chapters.sourcePressure: Balance high standards with deep support when helping others grow grit.
chapters.coreMove: Hold the line while making it clear the person is not alone at the line.
chapters.commonMisread: Thinking grit is produced by harshness, neglect, or unconditional ease.

chapters.title: The Playing Fields of Grit
chapters.sourcePressure: Use structured hard activities as training grounds for interest plus perseverance.
chapters.coreMove: Choose a hard thing you care about, finish the season, and let follow-through become identity.
chapters.commonMisread: Thinking any busy extracurricular or forced activity builds grit.

chapters.title: A Culture of Grit
chapters.sourcePressure: Show how groups make grit easier by turning standards into identity and language.
chapters.coreMove: Join or build a group where the normal answer to difficulty is sustained effort.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating grit as only an individual trait and ignoring peer norms.

chapters.title: Conclusion
chapters.sourcePressure: Put grit in proportion: develop it, use it, but do not mistake it for all of character.
chapters.coreMove: Keep a long commitment while knowing when values, fit, or opportunity cost justify quitting.
chapters.commonMisread: Thinking grit is the only virtue or that quitting is always failure.
